Losice Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Łosice, Poland

Demolished. Jewish settlement in Łosice dates to the end of the 17th century; by 1921, 2,708 (69.65%) were mostly murdered at Treblinka in 1942. This cemetery followed a May 30, 1690 privilege from King Jan III Sobieski granting Jews of Łódz 'the freedom to have a school and a cemetery in the town.' During WWII, the site held execution victims - Germans shot named individuals including Abram Bekierman in February 1943 and four more unnamed men that fall. Germans used matzevot to reinforce a military police station's yard; a 1960s '20th-Anniversary Park' with a stage, playground, and dance events was later built directly on the grounds. In 2003, pressure from Łosice-descended Jews and the Poland Jewish Cemetery Restoration Project recovered matzevot from the former gendarmerie post square; a 2007-2008 restoration fenced the site and built a lapidarium.
